name: Career
tip: your resume, applications, job search and portfolio
about: Your resume kept as data and typeset as a PDF in the theme you pick; jobs found on LinkedIn, Indeed, Glassdoor, Google and ZipRecruiter and ranked against your resume; for a job you name, a resume tailored to its posting and a cover letter - never inventing experience you do not have, and you press Submit yourself; a portfolio web page from your resume and the pictures and videos you give.
ask: What should I make - your resume, an application for a job, a job search or your portfolio?
subject: what he wants in one sentence of at most 24 words: the document or search and the role it is for

settings.label: Make
settings.tip: Resume: your resume as a typeset PDF. Apply to a job: for one posting (paste it, or its link), a tailored resume and a cover letter. Find jobs: postings found and ranked against your resume. Portfolio: a web page of your work. By the job: what your words ask for - 'find jobs ...' is Find jobs even when it names your resume

about.Resume: his resume itself, typeset as a PDF (make, update or restyle my resume)
about.Apply to a job: for one job posting he gives (pasted or a link): his resume tailored to it and a cover letter
about.Find jobs: job postings searched for and ranked against his resume (find jobs, openings, positions)
about.Portfolio: a web page showing his work and resume

settings.label: Resume look
settings.tip: RenderCV's themes: classic (blue headings, a clean default), engineeringresumes and sb2nov (dense, black and white, liked by technical recruiters), moderncv (a coloured side), engineeringclassic, harvard (the classic academic one), ember

settings.label: Paper
settings.tip: Letter for the US and Canada, A4 almost everywhere else

settings.label: Length
settings.tip: One page: the strongest points only (recruiters' usual ask under ten years of experience). Two pages: room for a long career

settings.label: Lead with
settings.tip: the kind of role the resume aims at, e.g. 'character artist for games' - the order and wording follow it; empty: what his experience shows best

settings.label: Search for
settings.tip: the job title and a skill or two; empty: from your resume

settings.label: Where
settings.tip: a city and state, or a country; empty: where your resume says you live

settings.label: Sites
settings.tip: All five adds Glassdoor and ZipRecruiter (slower, and they turn away searches more often)

recipe.title: Your resume as data
recipe.does: everything your files and words say about your work, kept as JSON Resume - the one source every page is made from

basics.label: the title he goes by
basics.summary: two or three sentences in his own voice

work.name: company
work.startDate: YYYY-MM, or YYYY when only the year is known
work.endDate: YYYY-MM or YYYY, empty for now
highlights: what he did and what came of it

args.brief: You keep a person's resume as JSON Resume data, in {language}. Fill it from his files and his words below: his name and contact, every job (company, title, dates as he gives them - YYYY-MM with a month, YYYY when he gives only the year, never a month he did not write - what he did), his education, skills grouped, projects, certificates, awards and languages. Every fact - a company, a date, a title, a number, a skill - comes from his files or his words; nothing is invented, rounded up or implied. Where something is not known it stays empty. Keep his own wording where it is good; make each highlight one line that starts with a strong verb and says what came of it, using only numbers he gave. Lead with what fits: {focus}. Length: {length} - for One page keep the newest and strongest highlights (at most four a job) and leave out what is old or weak; nothing is cut from the data for As long as it needs.

recipe.title: The resume, typeset
recipe.does: RenderCV sets the resume as a PDF in the look you picked; a picture of each page comes with it; a page more than the length you set stops it

recipe.title: What to search for
recipe.does: the search words and place, from your settings or your resume

shape.terms: the job title, two to four words

args.brief: Pick the job search for this person. The words: '{role}' when that is given, else the job title his resume points to next - his newest title, or the role his words ask for - two to four words, no skills or tools (job boards match every word, and each word more finds fewer postings). The place: '{place}' when that is given, else the city and region on his resume; empty for anywhere.

recipe.title: Find the postings
recipe.does: JobSpy searches the sites you picked for postings from the days you set

recipe.title: Ranked against your resume
recipe.does: each posting scored 1 to 5 against your resume, the reasons and the gaps, best first

args.brief: You are a recruiter who knows this person's resume well. Score every posting in jobs_brief.json from 1 (poor fit) to 5 (strong fit) against his resume: what it asks for that he has (name it from his resume), what it asks for that he lacks, and the level (junior to lead) against his years. Write Markdown in {language}: a heading, then a table of every posting best first - score, title linked to its url, company, place, pay when given - then for the five best a short paragraph each: why it fits, the gap to answer in a cover letter, and what to stress. Leave out none; invent nothing about a posting that it does not say.

recipe.title: The posting
recipe.does: the job's posting, from your message or its link: the role, the company and what it asks for

args.missing: the job posting - paste its text in your message, or its link (a page anyone can open without signing in)

shape.title: the job title
asks: each thing it requires or prefers, in its own words
shape.about: one or two sentences on the company or team, from the posting
shape.contact: the hiring manager's name if the posting gives one

args.brief: Take the job posting out of his request and the pages below: the title, the company, the place, the link, every requirement and preference in the posting's own words, the duties, a line about the company and the hiring manager's name if given. Only what the posting says. If there is no posting in his request or the pages (only a request to apply, or a page that is not a job), leave title and asks empty.

recipe.title: Tailored to the posting
recipe.does: your resume reordered and reworded for this one posting - nothing added that you do not have

basics.label: the title he goes by
basics.summary: two or three sentences in his own voice

work.name: company
work.startDate: YYYY-MM, or YYYY when only the year is known
work.endDate: YYYY-MM or YYYY, empty for now
highlights: what he did and what came of it

args.brief: Tailor this person's resume (resume.json below) to the job posting (posting.json below). Keep the same JSON Resume shape. Reorder highlights and skills so what the posting asks for comes first; reword a highlight to use the posting's own words where his experience truly matches; write basics.summary for this role; basics.label stays a title he holds or held (his current one, or a true description of what he does), never the posting's title when he has not had that job. Every fact - a company, a date, a title, a number, a skill - comes from his files or his words; nothing is invented, rounded up or implied. Where something is not known it stays empty. Never add a skill, tool, title or result that is not in resume.json - a requirement he does not meet stays unmet. Length: {length}.

recipe.title: The tailored resume, typeset
recipe.does: the tailored resume as a PDF in your look; a page more than the length you set stops it

recipe.title: The cover letter
recipe.does: a letter for this posting from what your resume shows

args.brief: Write this person's cover letter for the job posting (posting.json below), in {language}, about {letter_words} words, tone: {letter_tone}. Greeting (the hiring manager by name if the posting names one, else the team), then: why this role and company (from the posting), two or three things he has done that answer what it asks for most (from his resume, with his numbers), one honest line on a gap if the posting's main ask is one he lacks, a close that asks for a conversation, his name. Plain paragraphs separated by a blank line; no address block, no date, no placeholders in brackets. Every fact - a company, a date, a title, a number, a skill - comes from his files or his words; nothing is invented, rounded up or implied. Where something is not known it stays empty.

recipe.title: The letter, typeset
recipe.does: the letter as a PDF in the resume's type, your name and contact on top

recipe.title: The portfolio page
recipe.does: a web page from your resume and the pictures and videos you gave

args.summary: resume.pdf: your resume, typeset. resume.json keeps it as data: change it and ask again for any look.
matches.md: the postings ranked against your resume, best first, with links to apply.
resume_tailored.pdf and cover_letter.pdf for this posting. Read both before you send them - you press Submit.
portfolio/index.html: your portfolio page, ready to put on any web host.
